cluster_summary: This cluster contains vulnerabilities related to improper handling of IP addresses in proxy header parsing, canonicalization, and rate-limiting key generation. Common mistakes include assuming the first element of X-Forwarded-For is the client IP, failing to canonicalize IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses, misclassifying loopback addresses from proxies, and using full IPv6 addresses as rate-limiting keys without subnet masking.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-selected resource identifiers, object IDs, tenant IDs, or administrative action targets into sensitive read, write, mutation, deletion, workflow, or administrative operations on the selected resource. Report code paths where the authorization decision is not bound to both the current principal and the exact resource or tenant being affected. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 3 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should check ownership or tenant scope before the effect and carry that checked identity into the data access or mutation.

mechanism.missing_guard: the authorization decision is not bound to both the current principal and the exact resource or tenant being affected
mechanism.name: missing object-owner or tenant-scope authorization
mechanism.sink_shape: sensitive read, write, mutation, deletion, workflow, or administrative operations on the selected resource
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-selected resource identifiers, object IDs, tenant IDs, or administrative action targets
mechanism.typical_fix: check ownership or tenant scope before the effect and carry that checked identity into the data access or mutation

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Parse from the rightmost entry, skip trusted proxy IPs, and discard loopback addresses when the remote address is not loopback.
sub_patterns.name: Incorrect client IP extraction from X-Forwarded-For header due to assumption of first value and missing trust/loopback filtering
sub_patterns.root_cause: Code assumes first or leftmost value in X-Forwarded-For is the client IP, but proxies append real IP to the end; additionally, no filtering of trusted proxies or loopback addresses.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add trusted proxy configuration and proper client IP resolution; set local request flag to false if proxy hints are present or resolved client IP is not loopback.
sub_patterns.name: Proxied request loopback misclassification due to missing trusted proxy verification
sub_patterns.root_cause: Assumption that socket remote address of loopback with no proxy headers indicates a local request, without verifying trusted proxy chains.
